Support plans Services & enablement

Common Questions

What is an AI Credit?
An AI credit represents one unit of intelligent work performed by Datadog’s AI products listed above.
Do unused credits roll over?
AI Credits reset on the first day of each calendar month. Unused credits do not roll over to the next month.
What happens if I run out of AI Credits?
If your usage exceeds your purchased monthly bundle, additional credits are billed automatically at the On-Demand rate. You do not need to switch pricing models or top up manually.
How is AI Credits billed?
Annual, monthly, and on-demand plans are available. Annual and monthly plans are billed per 500 credits. On-demand is billed per individual credit. We can customize billing plans to meet your needs. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.

Common Questions

How is Code Coverage priced?
Code Coverage is priced per committer, per month, based on the maximum number of active committers during the billing period.
Do I need to pay separately if I already use Test Optimization or Code Security?
Eligible committers from Test Optimization and Code Security automatically include Code Coverage allotments. For example, for a team paying for 25 Test Optimization committers, they would get 25 Code Coverage committers at no additional cost.
How do you define a committer?
A committer means an active Git committer; they are identified through their Git author email address. A committer is counted towards billing if they commit at least 3 times in a given month.
What CI providers does Code Coverage support?
Code Coverage is compatible with GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps.
What languages does Code Coverage support for tests?
Code Coverage is language agnostic. Learn more about supported report formats.

Support Plans & Post Sales Services

From basic plans to bespoke offerings, Datadog offers the right level of support & services for any organization.

Support plans Services & enablement

Common Questions

Definitions
How do you define retention?

The retention period is the number of days your logs are searchable and analyzable. After this period, logs disappear from your index(es).

Logs removed from your index(es) do not have to be gone forever! Check out our Log Archives for long-term storage options.

I know my consumption in GB/day: how do I convert it into millions of log events?

Log events come in all shapes and sizes, which is precisely why we offer event-based pricing! We want to encourage rich logs to provide the most value.

The best way to get the number of log events during your Datadog trial is to run a count query over the last 24 hours and multiply by 30 days to estimate for the month. This can, of course, also be done in your current log management solution, if you have one.

What do the different compute sizes in Flex Logs mean? Which one is appropriate for me?
Compute is the querying capacity to run queries for Flex Logs. The compute size appropriate for you depends on the volume of data stored in the Flex Tier, the time window and complexity of your queries, and concurrency. For guidance on which compute size you should choose, see our documentation.
Supported Today
Can I subscribe to Log Management without using Datadog Infrastructure or APM?
Having all your infrastructure, APM, and log data under one roof is something we definitely encourage, but you can also subscribe only to Datadog’s Log Management. Learn how to configure only log collection here.
What retentions are available for on-demand customers?
For on-demand customers, the default retention is 15 days. If you have already created a Datadog account and would like to use a different retention, you can request a different retention at support@datadoghq.com
Do I have to choose only one type of retention between Standard Indexing and Flex Logs?
Your indexes can have Standard Tier retention only, Flex Tier retention only, or a combination of Standard and Flex Tier.
What is the difference between Standard Indexing and Flex Logs?
Flex Logs does not support monitors or Watchdog Insights. Standard Indexing supports everything.
What happens if I send an unexpectedly high volume of logs?

By committing to a monthly volume of logs, you aren’t rate-limited based on a single day’s volume. Send as much as you need on any given day without losing visibility. Assuming your average is lower on other days, your bill is unaffected.

In those cases where you have a big month, not to worry! You maintain complete visibility and pay for additional services (+50% of the annual price) only on the volume that exceeds your commitment.

Can I forward logs from one Datadog account to another?
This is currently not supported.
Best Practices
How can I manage my highly dynamic log volume in a cost-effective way without losing visibility?
We’ve designed our Log Management offer knowing from day 1 that managing large and fluctuating log volumes is a common problem. We have various innovative solutions for this, which you can learn more about from our dedicated article here.
When should I store logs in Standard Indexing vs Flex Logs?
Log events can be stored in Standard Indexing when you need them for real-time troubleshooting and in Flex Logs for ad-hoc, historical analysis and long term troubleshooting. See our documentation to learn more.
Billing
How are Flex Logs billed?
Flex Logs are metered on an hourly basis per million events stored. Each million events stored is billed for a minimum of 30 days, or a minimum of $0.05. For example, if one million logs are retained for 60 days, this will be charged for every 30 days that they are stored.
Is forwarding to S3 Archives, GCP Storage, and Azure Storage being billed?
No. Forwarding to S3 Archives, GCP Storage, and Azure Storage is included with $0.10 per ingested GB. However, forwarding to other destinations such as your external SIEM or BI vendor is billable starting at $0.25 per GB outbound per destination.
How is Rehydration billed?
When you rehydrate logs, Datadog scans the compressed logs in your archive for the time period you requested, and then indexes only log events that match your rehydration query. Datadog charges $0.10 per compressed GB of log data that is scanned. For any log events indexed from a rehydration, the cost is equal to your contracted indexing rates for the retention period selected for the rehydration.
How are log-based metrics billed?
Log-based metrics count towards your Custom Metrics allocation as outlined in your infrastructure plan.
Are there other billing options?
Annual and monthly plans are available. We can customize billing plans to meet your needs. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.
Security and Compliance
How can I be sure my data is secure?
Security is our top priority. This includes, TCP/SSL Strict Transport Security, agent-level scrubbing and SOC 2 compliance. Our Agent is open-source, which means it can be reviewed to ensure it meets your security requirements.

What is a feature flag?
A feature flag lets you enable, disable, or configure application behavior without redeploying code. Teams use feature flags to safely release features, run canary rollouts, and validate changes using real production traffic.
How is Datadog Feature Flags billed?

Feature Flags pricing is based on your monthly volume of flag configuration requests. Usage below 1 million monthly flag configuration requests is included at no cost. For usage above 1 million requests, pricing is billed per additional 1 million monthly flag configuration requests based on your selected billing model:

Monthly Flag Configuration Requests (MFCRs)Annual
cost per 1M MFCRs		Monthly
cost per 1M MFCRs		On-Demand
cost per 1M MFCRs
< 1MFreeFreeFree
1M - 10M$55$89$100
10M+$45$73$92
Do Feature Flags require APM?
Feature Flags can be used independently and don’t require licensing other Datadog products, but they leverage the APM and RUM SDKs for server-side and client-side implementations.
Can I investigate feature flag impact in APM, RUM, and Product Analytics?
Yes, but you must already be a customer of the relevant Datadog products. Feature flag evaluations are automatically correlated with Datadog APM, RUM, and Product Analytics data, allowing you to investigate errors, performance issues, and user behavior tied to specific flag states.
Can I migrate from another feature flag provider?
Yes. Datadog Feature Flags is built on the OpenFeature standard, which helps teams avoid vendor lock-in and simplifies migrations from existing providers. OpenFeature is a CNCF (Cloud Native Computing Foundation) project backed by major industry leaders, ensuring long-term portability and ecosystem support.
How reliable are Datadog Feature Flags?
Feature flag evaluations are designed to be highly reliable and safe by default. Datadog uses a globally distributed CDN-backed architecture to ensure low-latency access and resilience at scale. SDKs cache flag values locally and fall back to safe defaults if connectivity is interrupted, ensuring your application continues to operate even during network or service disruptions.
Which SDK languages are supported?
Datadog Feature Flags supports SDKs for common backend and frontend languages, including Java, JavaScript, Python, React, Go, Ruby, and mobile platforms. Learn more.
Is this available in all regions?
Yes. Feature Flags is available in all US-,  EU- and APAC-hosted accounts. Feature Flags are not available in GovCloud.
How can I start using Feature Flags?
Visit the Feature Flags documentation to get started with instrumenting and managing feature flags in your applications.

Support plans Services & enablement

Common Questions

How do you define a host?
A host is any physical or virtual OS instance that you monitor with Datadog. It could be a server, VM, or node (in the case of Kubernetes).
How do I monitor containers?
The Datadog Agent runs in a container alongside any number of other containers on a host. From there it can collect metrics from its neighboring containers and from the host itself. Depending on your plan, you can monitor 5 or 10 containers free for each host license. Additional containers will be billed at $0.002 per container per hour. In addition, you can purchase prepaid containers at $1 per container per month or $1.50 per container per month for DevSecOps Containers. Container monitoring is not available for Basic hosts.
What is a custom metric?
Datadog was designed to allow you to monitor your own custom applications and business metrics—not just your infrastructure. You can send any and all of your organization’s important metrics to Datadog for graphing, alerting, correlation, anomaly detection and more. Example uses: monitoring ad revenue, the rate at which shopping carts are abandoned, or the health of an in-game economy. Many customers find these metrics invaluable, especially when combined with infrastructure metrics.
How many custom metrics are allotted per host?
Datadog offers 100 custom metrics for every host monitored with Infrastructure Pro, or 200 custom metrics for every host monitored with Infrastructure Enterprise.
How do I get charged for additional custom metrics?
Custom metrics beyond your included allocation are billed based on usage. Contact us or reach out to your Sales or Customer Success rep for more details.
How does Datadog count and meter custom metrics?
Custom metrics are counted hourly and averaged monthly across your entire account, not on a per-host basis. For more details around Custom Metrics metering, please see our Custom Metrics Billing FAQ.
What is a custom event?
Datadog allows you to send custom events coming from your own custom applications such as custom-built deployment tools or scheduled maintenance jobs. This way, you can correlate any of these events with performance metrics, create monitors for alerting and enrich events at intake with processing pipelines to be queried alongside other standard events.
How many events are allotted per host?
Datadog offers 500 custom events for every host monitored with infrastructure monitoring for pro plan, or 1000 for enterprise plan. Custom events are averaged across your entire account, not just on a per-host basis. Beyond this limit, Datadog charges $2 for 100 000 custom events (billed annually or $3 on-demand), although it is rare for our customers to exceed the allotted volume.
How can I send custom metrics and events?

You can send Datadog custom metrics and events in three ways

  • The Datadog Agent ships with DogStatsD so you can submit custom metrics via the Agent's non-blocking API functions for many programming languages.
  • The Datadog Agent allows for the creation of custom integrations via plugins to the Agent. This plugin system allows the Agent to collect custom metrics on your behalf. Integrations which are contributed back to the Datadog Agent convert to standard metrics.
  • Datadog also has a full-featured API that you can send your metrics to—either directly over HTTP or with a language-specific library.
What compliance frameworks does DevSecOps support?
DevSecOps Pro and Enterprise allow you to track conformance to requirements of over 15 industry benchmarks including CIS, PCI DSS, SOC 2, and more.
How can I be sure my data is secure?
Security is our top priority. This includes, universal HTTPS, strong TLS configuration, and HTTP Strict Transport Security. Our Agent is open-source, which means it can be reviewed to ensure it meets your security requirements.
Are there other billing options?
Annual, monthly and hourly plans are available. We can customize billing plans to meet your needs. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ
Do you have special offerings for partners?
We’re always looking to partner with technology and service providers and resellers. See our Partners page for more.
What infrastructure monitoring is included in the Free tier?
When your free trial ends, you can choose to upgrade to a paid plan or move to the Free tier. On the Free tier, you get up to five Basic hosts with 1-day metric retention, at no cost. To monitor more hosts or retain data longer, upgrade to a paid plan at any time.
Can I mix and match infrastructure coverage?

You can choose one level of infrastructure coverage for your Datadog account: Pro, Enterprise, DevSecOps Pro, or DevSecOps Enterprise. If you choose Pro or Enterprise, you can also monitor a subset of your hosts with Basic level coverage.

The DevSecOps bundles cover your entire environment, and can’t be combined with standalone infrastructure, container, or cloud security products.

Support plans Services & enablement

Common Questions

APM APM Pro APM Enterprise
What counts as a billable APM host?
A billable APM host is a host that is actively generating traces that are submitted to the Datadog SaaS application, including, but not limited to, an OpenTelemetry Collector. This means that hosts running services that are not instrumented (e.g. databases, caches, queues and load-balancers) and are not generating traces submitted to the Datadog platform do not count as APM hosts even if APM is enabled on them.
Do I need Infrastructure Monitoring to use APM, APM Pro, or APM Enterprise?
No. APM, APM Pro, and APM Enterprise can be purchased standalone and do not require Infrastructure Monitoring. Standalone pricing is $36 for APM, $41 for APM Pro, and $47 for APM Enterprise, priced per host, per month, billed annually and available on-demand.
Is Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring required on every APM Host?
Only if you purchase APM using the Infrastructure Monitoring pricing model. In this case, every host running APM must also be subscribed to Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring. For example, if you have 10 APM hosts, those same 10 hosts must have Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring. This requirement applies to both committed and on-demand usage for all non-standalone APM tiers.
I am an existing APM customer. Can I switch to the APM Pro or APM Enterprise?
Yes. Existing APM customers have the option of changing their plan to APM Pro or APM Enterprise. Contact your Sales or Customer Success rep for help.
Can I purchase a mix of APM, APM Pro, and APM Enterprise hosts?
No. Customers can commit to only one of the plans across all their APM hosts, not a combination thereof.
Does a purchase of APM host include Universal Service Monitoring (USM) on that same host?
Yes. USM is included on the same host APM is purchased on, regardless of the APM tier. This means that Datadog will always discover, map, and monitor every new and/or non-instrumented service running on your APM hosts, automatically.
If I’m an existing USM customer and start using APM on the same host, will I be charged for both products?
No. If both USM and APM are purchased and/or installed on the same host, you will only pay the APM price on the host, based on your APM tier.
What languages does APM support?
Java, Python, Ruby, Go, Node, .NET and PHP. You can find the full list of supported languages and libraries in our documentation.
Can I add custom instrumentation on top of Datadog’s out-of-the-box instrumentation?
Yes. We provide auto-instrumentation for popular libraries and frameworks, but you can easily add custom instrumentation if desired.
Can I run APM with containers?
Yes, you can run APM in a containerized environment. The number of containers running on each host (node) does not impact the APM host-based price.
What is the difference between ingestion and retention?
Ingestion means sending your traces to Datadog and having all of them available for Live Search and Analytics for 15 minutes. Retention means storing your most important traces (e.g. error, high latency, or business-critical ones) and making them available for search and analysis during a retention period of your choice (15 days by default).
Can I ingest additional spans?

Yes. While we include 150GB per APM host by default for Ingested Spans, you can always ingest additional traces and spans for 15-minute live trace search and analytics at $0.10/GB.

Note: The allotted 150GB per host is summed over all the APM hosts. For example, if in a given month you have 2 APM hosts and one ingests 250GBs and the other 50GBs (300GB in total), you will not be billed for ingestion that month.

Can I retain (index) additional spans and modify the retention period?

Yes. While we include 1 million Indexed Spans per APM host with 15-day retention by default, you can always retain additional spans.

For additional Indexed Spans, we offer the following retention periods:

  • 7-day retention at $1.27 per million spans per month (billed annually or $1.91 on-demand)
  • 15-day retention at $1.70 per million spans per month (billed annually or $2.55 on-demand)
  • 30-day retention at $2.50 per million spans per month (billed annually or or $3.75 on-demand)

If you need longer retention, please reach out to your Customer Success or Sales rep to customize your plan.

Note 1: The allotted 1 million Indexed Spans per host is summed across all your APM hosts. For example, if in a given month you have 2 APM hosts and you index 1.5 million spans from one and 0.5 million from the other (2 million in total), you will not be billed for indexing that month.

Note 2: Indexed Spans that are auto-retained by Datadog do not count towards the 1 million Indexed Spans that are allotted per host.

How does on-demand billing of ingested and indexed spans differ from my committed plan?

On-demand use of APM is counted on an hourly basis. Both ingested and indexed span allotment are metered each hour and are not aggregated across all use throughout the month.

This means that ingested and indexed span use that goes over the associated APM Host allotment in the same hour will increase billing regardless of span use during other times.

What are the hourly span allotments and on-demand pricing?

For every host hour, customers get an hourly allotment corresponding to a share of the monthly allotment (150 GB for ingested spans and 1M indexed) split evenly by hour by month in the current year. For example, in January, for every host hour, customers get an allotment of 0.205 GB (150 GB / (365 * 24 / 12)) for ingested spans and 1369 indexed spans (1 M / (365 * 24 / 12)).

For additional volume, in a given hour, customers will be charged $0.10 per additional GB of ingested spans and the indexed spans rate for every additional 1M indexed spans.

Do I have to ingest and/or retain 100% of my traces?
No. Updates to trace ingestion and retention can be made directly in the UI giving customers full control over their data and costs. For additional information, view the Ingestion Controls and Trace Retention documentation.
Does trace sampling impact the accuracy of RED metrics?
No, the listed APM price includes RED metrics (requests, errors, duration). Regardless of any sampling rate (default or custom), RED metrics are always calculated based on 100% of application traffic.
How are span-based metrics billed?
Span-based metrics are counted towards your Custom Metrics allocation as outlined in your infrastructure plan.
Are there other billing options?
Annual, monthly and hourly plans are available. We can customize billing plans to meet your needs. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.
Can I run APM with Mobile Devices (Android, IoS etc.,)?
Yes, We have the Tracing Libraries that support Android and iOS applications. Running the Datadog Agent is not required for Mobile Devices. The APM price is based on the ingested and indexed spans volume (note: by default, spans are indexed for 15 days).
Can I use APM on Edge Devices?
APM is available for Edge Devices, such as Point of Sale (POS) systems, in-store kiosks, industrial devices, and entertainment systems. The same APM features are included, at a reduced price per device with lower ingest and retention allotments. Please contact your Customer Success or Sales rep with details of your use case.

A billable APM host is a host that is actively generating traces that are submitted to the Datadog SaaS application, including, but not limited to, an OpenTelemetry Collector. This means that hosts running services that are not instrumented (e.g. databases, caches, queues and load-balancers) and are not generating traces submitted to the Datadog platform do not count as APM hosts even if APM is enabled on them.
Do I need Infrastructure Monitoring to use APM, APM Pro, or APM Enterprise?
No. APM, APM Pro, and APM Enterprise can be purchased standalone and do not require Infrastructure Monitoring. Standalone pricing is $36 for APM, $41 for APM Pro, and $47 for APM Enterprise, priced per host, per month, billed annually and available on-demand.
Is Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring required on every APM Host?
Only if you purchase APM using the Infrastructure Monitoring pricing model. In this case, every host running APM must also be subscribed to Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring. For example, if you have 10 APM hosts, those same 10 hosts must have Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring. This requirement applies to both committed and on-demand usage for all non-standalone APM tiers.
What is Data Streams Monitoring and how does it work?
Datadog Data Streams Monitoring (DSM) allows you to track and improve the performance of event-driven applications that use Kafka and RabbitMQ. DSM automatically maps dependencies between all services and queues, measures latency between them, and provides additional health metrics, such as consumer lag, across your streaming data pipeline to help you monitor it end to end.
What counts as a billable DSM host?
A billable Data Streams Monitoring host is a host that has the Datadog Agent installed and producer and consumer services that are running on it and instrumented for DSM. Visit our documentation for additional setup information.
What kind of billing plan do I need to run Data Streams Monitoring?
Every billable DSM host requires the purchase of Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring, regardless if it is combined with APM. Annual, month-to-month, and on-demand billing plans are available. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.
Can I purchase Data Streams Monitoring not as part of an APM plan?
Yes, Data Streams Monitoring can be purchased on top of Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring hosts starting at $15 per host per month with an annual commitment.
Can I purchase APM Pro for a portion of my hosts and individual standalone products for the rest of my hosts?
No. Customers can commit to only one of the plans across all their APM hosts, not a combination thereof. That said, APM-only customers can purchase Data Streams Monitoring and/or Continuous Profiler on a portion of their hosts, and APM Pro customers can purchase Continuous Profiler on a portion of their hosts.
What Technologies do you support?
DSM currently supports Java, Go, .NET/C# for Kafka and Java and Go for RabbitMQ. Support for additional technologies and programming languages is coming soon.
How long is DSM data retained for?
Map history is stored for 30 days and all metrics are retained for 15 months.
What counts as a billable APM host?
A billable APM host is a host that is actively generating traces that are submitted to the Datadog SaaS application, including, but not limited to, an OpenTelemetry Collector. This means that hosts running services that are not instrumented (e.g. databases, caches, queues and load-balancers) and are not generating traces submitted to the Datadog platform do not count as APM hosts even if APM is enabled on them.
Do I need Infrastructure Monitoring to use APM, APM Pro, or APM Enterprise?
No. APM, APM Pro, and APM Enterprise can be purchased standalone and do not require Infrastructure Monitoring. Standalone pricing is $36 for APM, $41 for APM Pro, and $47 for APM Enterprise, priced per host, per month, billed annually and available on-demand.
Is Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring required on every APM Host?
Only if you purchase APM using the Infrastructure Monitoring pricing model. In this case, every host running APM must also be subscribed to Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring. For example, if you have 10 APM hosts, those same 10 hosts must have Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring. This requirement applies to both committed and on-demand usage for all non-standalone APM tiers.
What is Continuous Profiler?
Continuous Profiler is a tool to observe and analyze code-level performance in your production environment at all times with minimal overhead. It allows developers to identify and optimize the most resource-consuming methods in their code. We provide comprehensive documentation and encourage you to take a read.
What counts as a billable Continuous Profiler host?
A billable Continuous Profiler host is a host that has profiling installed and enabled according to Datadog’s runtime-specific setup instructions (example) and submits profiles to the Datadog SaaS application.
What kind of billing plan do I need to run APM Enterprise?
Every billable Continuous Profiler host requires the purchase of Pro or Enterprise Infrastructure Monitoring, regardless if it is combined with APM. The price includes 4 containers running profiled applications per host, summed across all Profiled hosts. Every additional container costs $2. Annual, month-to-month, and on-demand billing plans are available. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.
I am an existing Continuous Profiler customer. Can I switch to the APM Enterprise plan?
Yes. Existing Continuous Profiler customers have the option of changing their plan to APM Enterprise starting at $40 per host per month. Contact your Sales or Customer Success rep for help.'
Can I purchase Continuous Profiler standalone?
Yes, Continuous Profiler can be purchased standalone at $19 per profiled host per month with an annual commitment. Month-to-month and on-demand plans are also available at $23 per profiled host per month or $0.004 per hour. Contact us or reach out to your Sales or Customer Success rep for more details.
Can I purchase APM Enterprise for a portion of my hosts and individual standalone products for the rest of my hosts?
No. Customers can commit to only one of the plans across all their APM hosts, not a combination thereof. That said, APM-only customers can purchase Continuous Profiler and/or Data Streams Monitoring on a portion of their hosts, and APM Pro customers can purchase Continuous Profiler on a portion of their hosts.
How do you define a profiled host?
A profiled host is a physical or virtual operating system instance which is running a profiled application. To be profiled, the host would need to have the agent installed and profiling enabled. When combined with APM, every APM host is also a profiler host, and vice versa. The same logic applies to profiled containers. For more information visit our Billing FAQ.
Which languages does Continuous Profiler support?
Continuous Profiler supports Java, .NET, Go, Python, Ruby, .Node.js, and PHP. Support for C, C++, and Rust is in beta.
How does Datadog Continuous Profiler work?
Our profilers constantly collect representative samples of all stack traces, aggregate them over a 60-second time period and forwards them through the Datadog agent. This is done continuously in one-minute intervals which means you will never lose code-level visibility in your services. To profile your services, simply import our profiling library or enable an environment variable flag when you run the APM tracer.
How do you ensure minimal performance impact in production?
We use the latest, most cutting-edge technologies, such as the JDK Flight Recorder, to ensure that performance impact is minimal even with full production workloads. Additionally, our profilers do not interrupt or interfere with any of your service requests hence we introduce no additional request latency.
How is profiling different from tracing?
Tracing measures latency of requests across services in distributed systems, whereas profiling provides deeper insights on all that happened on the code level of the services.
What are the benefits of Datadog Continuous Profiler?
Continuous Profiler is tightly integrated with the rest of the Datadog platform and it extends our seamless correlations between metrics, traces, and logs to the code level. This is extremely useful for code performance optimization, cost savings on cloud provider bills, and reducing request latency for improved user experience.
What types of profiles are available?
CPU, Memory, Lock, Wall Time, Disk IO, Socket IO, Goroutines, Exceptions and many more profile types are available and may vary by programming language. For more information visit our documentation page.
Are there other billing options?
Annual, monthly and hourly plans are available. We can customize billing plans to meet your needs. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.

Workload Protection can be purchased in addition to Infrastructure Monitoring, and is already included if CSM Enterprise is purchased.
What counts as a billable host?
A host is any physical or virtual OS instance that you monitor with Datadog. It could be a server, VM, node (in the case of Kubernetes) or App Service Plan instance (in the case of Azure App Services).
How do I monitor containers and Kubernetes workloads?
In containerized environments, the Datadog agent runs in a container alongside any number of other containers on a host. From there it monitors system activity for all running containers and for the host itself. Depending on your plan, you can monitor 4 containers free for each host license. Additional containers will be billed at $0.002 per container per hour. In addition, you can purchase prepaid containers at $1 per container per month.
What environments does Workload Protection support?
We support most major Linux distributions, Windows Servers, and container runtimes including Docker and Kubernetes to provide unparalleled visibility into your workloads.

How do you define a committer?

Common Questions

What is Continuous Testing?

Datadog Continuous Testing is a comprehensive toolkit in the development cycle that offers integration and end-to-end testing with codeless test setup, self-healing capability, and seamless integration with CI providers (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, CircleCI, GitLab, and Jenkins) and collaboration tools to help you ship high-quality features to your users quickly.

Running tests in your CI/CD pipelines today is included with your API and Browser Testing test runs, and tests will run sequentially (one after another). If you would like to increase the speed of testing in your CI/CD pipelines, you can purchase additional Parallel Testing speed (parallelization), which makes some tests run at the same time.

For example, 1 Parallel Testing additional speed offers an additional parallel slot, allowing you to run 2 tests in parallel; 2 Parallel Testing additional speed offers 2 additional parallel slots, allowing you to run 3 tests in parallel; and so on. This helps you run more tests in parallel (at the same time), and reduce the overall execution speed of your test suite.

Am I limited to a certain number of test runs based on my additional parallelization?

No. With Parallel Testing, you can run as many tests as you need in your CI/CD pipelines. Parallelization ensures you can run more of those tests at the same time, and ultimately reduce the duration of testing in your CI/CD pipelines.

For example, if you want to run 100 tests in a CI pipeline and each test takes 10 seconds to run:

  • WITHOUT parallelization, your tests will run sequentially and your pipeline will take roughly 17 minutes to complete.
  • WITH parallelization, if you purchase (for example) an additional speed of 4 Parallel Testing, your 100 tests will run over a total of 5 parallel slots, and your pipeline will now take roughly 3 minutes to complete.

Note: In both cases, your 100 test runs will contribute to your API or Browser Testing test run quotas.

Can I reuse my Synthetic tests that I use to monitor my production environments?
Yes. With Parallel Testing, you can use the same Synthetic tests you have configured for production monitoring across all of your staging, QA, and pre-production environments. Through variable overrides and custom configuration values, you can benefit from one test throughout your entire software development lifecycle.
What are parallel tests?

Parallel tests are tests that run simultaneously in your continuous integration and delivery pipelines to ensure that you can:

  • Reduce pipeline duration and ship new features faster
  • Increase development confidence and speed of delivery
  • Have complete test coverage and reduce the volume of production-breaking bugs from reaching your codebase

As an example, if you needed to run 60 tests and each test took one minute to run, it would take you one hour to run those tests sequentially. However, running those tests in parallel with a parallelization value of 60, you could run all your tests at the same time and within one minute, saving you 59 minutes to tackle other business-critical tasks. That's the power of Parallel Testing.

Can I see the full trace of a test if I also use Datadog APM?
Yes! If you instrument your services with APM, you will have a complete 360-degree visibility into your applications and services—from your frontend user experience right through to your backend trace. Find more information here.
What counts as a browser test run?
Each simulation of a web transaction (up to 25 steps) counts as a single browser test run. A single test containing 50 steps would count as two test runs on each execution. For example, running a 60-step test (three test runs) every 15 minutes from five different locations and two different devices equates to 120 test runs in one hour.
How do subtests count toward billing?
Subtests are simply a set of steps within a browser test. Therefore, we count a subtest as part of the overall browser test execution. For example, if you set up a browser test with only three subtests and each subtest had five steps, that would amount to a total of 15 steps, or one browser test run.

    Common Questions

    What is a seat?

    A seat is a license to actively participate in on-call or incident management in Datadog. You claim a seat the first time you take an action that needs one, and billing admins can assign seats in advance so your team has access before they need it.

    For more information on how seats are assigned, claimed, and billed, see the Incident Response billing documentation.

    What is an On-Call seat?

    You need an On-Call seat to:

    • Participate in an on-call schedule
    • Be included in an escalation policy
    • Set up notification preferences to receive pages

    You do not need a seat to page another team or view existing pages, escalation policies, teams, or schedules.

    What is an Incident Management seat?

    You need an Incident Management seat to:

    • Modify an incident, including changes to its status, severity, or any custom field
    • Delete an incident
    • Add a comment, graph, or link to an incident timeline
    • Assign a task to someone within an incident (the assignee does not need a seat)
    • Assign a responder to a user-defined role within an incident (the assignee does need a seat)

    You do not need a seat to create incidents, view incidents, or join incident channels.

    Posting a message in a connected Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Google Chat channel does not require a seat either, including when that message syncs to the incident timeline. You need a seat only to act through the Datadog integration in Slack or Teams (for example, using action buttons) and to add comments, graphs, or links directly to a timeline in Datadog.

    What is an Incident Response seat?
    An Incident Response seat is one license covering both On-Call and Incident Management. If your organization commits to Incident Response, anyone who meets either the On-Call or the Incident Management criteria claims a single Incident Response seat instead of one seat in each product.
    Do people get double charged if they work in more than one org?
    No. Datadog charges on unique seats across the organizations where someone has an account, and deduplicates by the user’s email address.
    Should I buy On-Call and Incident Management separately, or the Incident Response bundle?

    Separately: On-Call at $20 per seat, per month, and Incident Management at $30, each seated and billed independently. Choose this when the two groups barely overlap, such as a large on-call rotation plus a handful of incident commanders.

    The Incident Response bundle: at $40 per seat, per month, gives you one seat pool covering both products. Choose this when the same people do both, since it avoids paying for two seats per person.

    What happens if someone without a seat tries to act on an incident?
    They are not blocked from creating, viewing, or joining incidents, since none of those need a seat. If they try an action that does need one, Datadog prompts them to claim a seat. If all your committed seats are in use, the claim still succeeds and the extra seat bills at your on-demand rate. To control which users can take those actions, see the incident management role permissions.
    If I rotate people through On-Call, what do I pay for?

    You pay for the highest number of seats assigned at one time, not for everyone who has ever held one. Bear in mind that unassigning someone does not free the seat immediately: it stays billable for the period you unassigned it in and drops off the next cycle. Swapping a seat between two people inside the same period therefore counts as two billable seats that period.

    If you rotate frequently, size your committed seats against everyone who will hold a seat during a billing period rather than the number on call at once.

    For more information on releasing seats when people or teams no longer need On-Call access, see Offboarding teams and users from Datadog On-Call.

    Can I remove seats?

    You can unassign a seat yourself at any time in Seat Management, which stops future charges for it. The seat stays billable for the period you unassigned it in and drops off the next cycle.

    Reducing your committed seat count is a contract change and takes effect at renewal. Unassigning people below your committed count does not reduce your committed spend.

    How can I see who is using a seat?

    Go to Plan & Usage → Seat Management. You will find a tab for each product you have enabled, your seats in use against your committed count, and a table of everyone holding a seat with their email and assignment date. You can search by name or email.

    If you see On-Call seats in use but no schedules, teams, or escalation policies configured, that is expected. Setting up notification preferences to receive pages occupies a seat on its own. On-Call admins can open the Notification Preferences settings page to see which schedules or escalation policies someone belongs to.

    Clearing someone’s notification preferences does not release their seat. To release a seat, unassign them in Seat Management.

    Does my seat price include telephony costs?
    Yes. Your seat price includes SMS and voice paging costs.
    Is there a limit on the number of schedules, escalation policies, incidents, or postmortems that a user or org can create?
    No, seat holders have access to create unlimited schedules, escalation policies, incidents, and postmortems.
    What external tools does Datadog Incident Response integrate with?

    One connected system, built on the tools you already use, to power every stage of incident response, from initial alert through post-incident follow-up.

    • Chat: Slack, MS Teams, Google Chat
    • Ticketing: Jira, Linear, ServiceNow
    • Video conferencing: Zoom, MS Teams, Google Meet
    • Alerts: 30+ native integrations to trigger On-Call pages

    Check out our Incident Management and On-Call docs for more information.

    Can I use Datadog Incident Management without using other Datadog products?
    Datadog Incident Management can be used as a standalone solution for your team, or as a central in-app hub to accelerate remediation and streamline existing workflows in Datadog.
    Can I use Datadog Incident Response without other Datadog products?
    Yes. On-Call and Incident Management each work on their own, with no other Datadog product required. You can also run them as a hub inside Datadog, so responders move from an alert to the incident to the underlying traces, logs, and metrics without leaving the platform.
    What are Incident Automations?
    Incident Automations are Workflow Automation executions that incidents trigger in Datadog. You can run them manually, on a schedule, or automatically in response to events in Incident Management, such as an incident status change or a timeline update. See our documentation for more.

    Common Questions

    How does Datadog Error Tracking work?
    Error Tracking automatically groups uncaught exceptions found in certain error events (from APM traces, RUM sessions, standalone frontend errors, and logs) across frontend and backend applications into issues with rich debug context.
    How is Error Tracking billed?

    Error Tracking is billed according to your monthly volume of errors. Monthly error volumes below 50k errors will be billed at the flat rate of $25 per month or $36 on-demand. For monthly error volumes over 50k, the cost per 1,000 errors will be billed as follows:

    Error Tracking pricing tiersAnnual
    cost per 1k errors, per month    		Monthly
    cost per 1k errors, per month    		On-Demand
    cost per 1k errors, per month
    > 50k - 100k errors$0.25$0.30$0.38
    > 100k - 500k errors$0.21$0.25$0.32
    > 500k - 10M errors$0.17$0.20$0.26
    > 10M - 20M errors$0.12$0.14$0.22
    > 20M+ errors$0.10$0.12$0.18
    Which errors are indexed and billed for Error Tracking?
    Standalone frontend errors collected outside of RUM sessions, standalone backend errors collected outside of APM traces, and errors originating from logs (with certain attributes) are billed for Error Tracking. To learn more about instrumenting Error Tracking and Error Tracking attributes view our documentation.
    Can I filter errors eligible for Error Tracking?
    Yes. You can use Error Tracking Rules to include and exclude certain errors that are ingested and billed by Error Tracking. We also offer rate limiting capabilities to safeguard against unexpected costs by allowing you to set a budget, ensuring your bill remains predictable and under control. You can also view a rolling 24-hour volume estimate in-app.
    Which programming languages does Error Tracking support?
    Browser Errors support JavaScript and TypeScript. Mobile Errors support Native iOS, Native Android, and React Native. Backend Errors support Java, NodeJS, .NET, Python, Ruby, Go, PHP, and C++.
    I’m an existing Datadog APM and/or Real User Monitoring (RUM) customer. Do I need to pay for Error Tracking?
    No. Error Tracking is included for errors collected as part of APM traces and RUM sessions at no additional cost. Error Tracking for Logs requires the Log Management product with indexing.
    Is this available in all regions?
    Yes. Error Tracking is available in all EU- and US-hosted accounts.
    How can I start using Error Tracking?
    Visit the Error Tracking documentation and start sending your backend or browser and mobile application errors to Error Tracking. Error Tracking can be enabled in-app.

    Common Questions

    What counts as a “session” in Product Analytics pricing?
    Similar to Real User Monitoring, a session is a continuous period of user interaction on your website or app, typically grouped by user activity and timeout thresholds. A session is a user journey on your web application. It expires after 15 minutes of inactivity and lasts up to 4 hours. For a detailed explanation of user sessions, please see our docs.
    Is Product Analytics available for both Browser and Mobile Applications?
    Yes – Product Analytics is available for Browser and Mobile Applications.
    Can I use Product Analytics without enabling Session Replay?
    Yes—Product Analytics works independently, allowing you to analyze conversion, retention, and workflow metrics without recording visual replays. That said, pairing it with Session Replay gives you powerful visual context to see exactly why users drop off or struggle, making it easier to validate hypotheses and troubleshoot faster.
    How long is my data retained?
    Behavioral data in Product Analytics is retained for a minimum of 15 months, so you can analyze long-term adoption and validate the lasting impact of product changes over time. By default, Session Replays will be retained for 30 days.
    Can I get more than 15 months retention?
    Yes – please reach out to your dedicated Datadog account team for more information.
    How is Product Analytics different from Real User Monitoring?
    RUM focuses on frontend performance—like load times and errors—while Product Analytics measures user behavior, including conversions, drop-offs, and feature adoption. Both use the same SDKs, but Product Analytics includes 15-month retention for behavioral data. They can be used separately or together for a complete view.
    Does purchasing Product Analytics increase the retention period for Session Replays compared to RUM alone?
    No — Session Replays have a standard 30-day retention period whether accessed through RUM or Product Analytics. If you’re interested in extending your replay retention, please reach out to your Datadog account team to discuss available options.
    Will I get double-billed on Session Replays if I purchase both RUM and Product Analytics?
    No — Session Replays are only billed once, even if you’re using them across both RUM and Product Analytics.
    Is Product Analytics available in all regions?
    Product Analytics is available for all US-hosted and EU-hosted Datadog accounts. It is not yet supported on GovCloud, but we’re actively working toward future availability.
    Should I export RUM data, Product Analytics data, or both to my warehouse?

    It depends on who will use the data and what they need to answer:

    1. Export Product Analytics data if your product, growth or data teams want to analyze user behavior and business outcomes, such as feature adoption, funnel conversion, retention or engagement by customer segment. It includes server-side events, labeled actions, and user and account profiles, so you can connect user behavior to complete user profiles.
    2. Export RUM data if your engineering teams want to analyze app performance and reliability in the warehouse, such as page load times, errors, failed requests or crash rates. RUM data is detailed, technical and tied to individual sessions.

    Common Questions

    How does AI Guard work?
    AI Guard sits inline with your AI applications and evaluates the full conversation context in real time. It inspects every prompt, response, tool call, MCP call, and API interaction against each agent’s behavioral baseline, session history, and the data and tools it can reach, blocking malicious activity in milliseconds before sensitive data leaves your environment. Please refer to the documentation to learn more.
    What languages and frameworks does AI Guard support?
    Automatic integrations (no code changes): Python (LangChain, OpenAI, Anthropic), Node.js (AI SDK, OpenAI, Anthropic), and Ruby (RubyLLM). Manual integrations: Python (Amazon Strands, LiteLLM Proxy). Any provider or language is supported via the HTTP API. Supported models include OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google VertexAI, and Azure.
    Is AI Guard a standalone offering? Can AI Guard be purchased separately?
    Yes. AI Guard is a standalone product. It is billed separately and does not require any other Datadog product. AI Guard includes an APM allotment, so customers without APM aren’t billed for the ingestion of traces AI Guard emits.
    What counts as a billable AI Guard token?
    A billable token is an input token submitted to AI Guard for evaluation. Tokens include the full conversation context sent to AI Guard evaluators, including user prompts, LLM responses, and tool call arguments and results. Failed evaluations (service unavailable) are not counted.
    Do I have to deploy AI Guard across all my services and agents?
    No. AI Guard can be enabled per service, environment, or agent, and policies can be configured independently for each.
    What billing options are available?
    Annual, monthly, and hourly (on-demand) plans are available. Prepaid drawdown is also supported. We can customize billing plans to meet your needs. For a detailed explanation of billing, please see our Billing FAQ.
    Are multi-year or volume discounts available?
    Annual commitment unlocks the lowest rate. Volume tiering is available via Deal Desk for high-volume customers. Prepaid drawdown is supported.
    Is AI Guard available in all regions?
    Yes. AI Guard is available in all regions except US1-FED.
    Do you have special offerings for partners?
    We’re always looking to partner with technology and service providers and resellers. See our Partners page for more.

    Common Questions

    How is Datadog Experiments priced?
    Datadog Experiments is priced based on the number of successfully launched experiments. An experiment is considered successfully launched—and billable—once it reaches at least 500 total subjects and runs for a minimum of 3 days.
    Do I need Datadog Feature Flags to use Experiments?
    You can use Datadog Feature Flags to run Experiments end-to-end or connect your own flagging system via warehouse native experimentation.
    Do I need Product Analytics to use Experiments?
    No, you do not need Product Analytics to run experiments. You can run experiments and measure results directly in your data warehouse using warehouse-native mode. Customers who use RUM and/or Product Analytics alongside Experiments can measure performance and behavioral impact alongside their business metrics.
    How is this different from traditional A/B testing tools?
    Datadog Experiments lets you measure the signals that matter — starting with business metrics directly from your native data warehouse. Within the broader Datadog platform, you can go one step further to unify experiments with observability and product analytics data to measure performance metrics like latency and errors, analyze user behavior with funnels and frustration signals, and connect to warehouse-native business metrics such as revenue, retention, and LTV.
    Do Datadog Experiments support advanced statistical methods?
    Yes, Datadog Experiments supports multiple statistical models and includes built-in variance reduction (CUPED) to help improve experiment sensitivity and reduce time to results.
    Can I monitor performance impact during experiments?
    Yes, you can connect RUM signals to your experiments to detect performance regressions that are correlated with specific experiment variants. Monitor key metrics like latency, errors, and Core Web Vitals in real time to understand the technical impact of every change you ship.
    How are Feature Flags and Experiments related?
    Feature Flags power the rollout of randomized variants to your users. Experiments build on top of Feature Flags to measure the impact of those variants with statistical rigor. When you purchase Datadog Experiments, you’ll receive an included allotment of Feature Flag credits, so you can get started quickly without additional setup.
    How can I start using Experiments?
    You can simply navigate to the Experiments page in Datadog, define the metrics you want to measure, and create your experiment. When you’re ready to launch, attach it to a Feature Flag and deploy your variants. For detailed setup instructions and best practices, learn more in our documentation.

    Common Questions

    AWS Fargate AWS Lambda AWS Step Functions Azure App Service Azure Container Apps Azure Functions Google Cloud Run GKE Autopilot
    How do you define an active application instance?
    Active instances for Fargate are the number of unique running Fargate tasks (ECS) or Fargate pods (EKS) that were observed in an active state during at least one 5-minute metering interval, averaged across the month.
    Is Tracing included in Fargate Monitoring?
    Tracing applications running on ECS Fargate or EKS Fargate is supported via the add on Serverless Apps APM product. It can be enabled with the Datadog Agent and adding a tracing library to your application.
    What metrics are included in Serverless Workload Monitoring?
    Each active application instance includes an allotment of 20 ingested custom metrics and 20 indexed custom metrics under application monitoring. The APM add-on offering provides 30GB of Ingested Spans and Indexed Spans allotment to 195k. See APM common questions for additional retention periods.
    Can I control how many requests are traced?
    Yes, you can control the percentage of Fargate requests that generate APM data by configuring your tracing settings.
    How do I track my usage?
    Datadog’s Plan & Usage page shows all active app instances broken down by workload. You can also view all ECS Fargate workloads in the ECS view and EKS workloads in the Kubernetes view in Datadog.
    How do you define an active function?
    Datadog bills based on the average number of functions per hour across the month for your accounts. Every hour, Datadog records the number of functions that were executed one or more times and monitored by your Datadog account. At the end of the month, Datadog charges by calculating the average of the hourly number of functions recorded. For example, if you invoked a function only once during a month, your bill will be 1 function / 720 hours * $5.
    How do you define a traced invocation?
    Datadog creates a top-level Lambda span for every Lambda invocation that is traced. Your bill is based on the sum of AWS Lambda invocations connected to an ingested APM trace in a given month. You will also be billed for the total number of indexed spans submitted to the Datadog APM service exceeding the bundled quantity at the end of the month.
    Can I control how many invocations are traced?
    Yes, Datadog allows you to control the percentage of Lambda function invocations that generate APM data.
    Can Serverless Functions APM be purchased without Serverless Workload Monitoring?
    No, Serverless Functions APM is an optional add-on for serverless functions sending metrics to Datadog via Serverless Workload Monitoring.
    What is allotted with Serverless Functions APM?
    Span Ingestion: 50GB Ingested Spans per 1M traced invocations; then $0.10/GB. Span Retention: 300 thousand Indexed Spans per 1M traced invocations; then $1.70 per 1 million Indexed Spans with 15-day retention (billed annually or $2.55 on-demand). See APM common questions for additional retention periods.
    What AWS Lambda runtimes do you support?
    Python, Node.js, Go, Ruby, Java, and .NET
    Can I monitor other AWS services used alongside my Lambda functions?
    Yes, Datadog has an easy to set up AWS integration which immediately pulls in metrics and more from 85+ AWS services, including Amazon API Gateway, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS AppSync, Amazon SQS, Amazon Kinesis, and AWS Step Functions.
    What security capabilities are available for AWS Lambda?
    Datadog allows you to detect meaningful threats on your applications running on AWS Lambda, and block attacks in your AWS Web Application Firewall (WAF) using Workflow Automation. Learn more about application security with our documentation.
    How do you define an active AWS Step Function?
    Datadog bills based on the average number of AWS Step Functions per hour across the month for your accounts. Every hour, Datadog records the number of Step Functions that were executed one or more times and monitored by your Datadog account. At the end of the month, Datadog charges by calculating the average of the hourly number of AWS Step Functions recorded. For example, if you invoked a function only once during a month, your bill will be 1 function / 720 hours * $5.
    How do you define a span for AWS Step Functions?
    Datadog bills based on the sum of AWS Step Function State transitions connected to an ingested APM trace in a given month. You will also be billed for the total number of indexed spans submitted to the Datadog APM service exceeding the bundled quantity at the end of the month. Any spans that are linked to the Step Function state, such as a Lambda invocation span, is billed additionally. See AWS lambda pricing for more details.
    Can I control how many invocations are traced?
    Yes, Datadog allows you to control the percentage of AWS Step Function invocations that generate APM data.
    Can Serverless Functions APM be purchased without Serverless Workload Monitoring?
    No, Serverless Functions APM is an optional add-on for serverless functions sending metrics to Datadog via Serverless Workload Monitoring.
    What is allotted with Serverless Functions APM?
    Span Ingestion: 50GB Ingested Spans per 1M traced invocations; then $0.10/GB. Span Retention: 300 thousand Indexed Spans per 1M traced invocations; then $1.70 per 1 million Indexed Spans with 15-day retention (billed annually or $2.55 on-demand). See APM common questions for additional retention periods.
    What if I am sending both AWS Lambda Spans and AWS Step Function Spans?
    AWS Lambda spans will be billed separately from AWS Step Function Spans. However, you can still link traces from AWS Lambda and Step Functions together to get end-to-end step function execution visibility.
    Can I monitor other Serverless AWS services used alongside my Step Functions?
    Yes, you can monitor AWS Lambda functions with the Datadog Extension to get even deeper visibility into your Serverless workloads. Datadog also has an easy to set up AWS integration which immediately pulls in metrics and more from 85+ AWS services, including Amazon API Gateway, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS AppSync, Amazon SQS, Amazon Kinesis
    How do you define an active application instance?
    Active application instances for Azure App Service are the number of unique web app or function app instances that were observed in an active state during at least one 5-minute metering interval, averaged across the month.
    Is Tracing included in Container App Monitoring?
    Tracing Azure App Service applications is supported via the add on Serverless Apps APM product. It can be enabled with the Datadog Serverless Agent and adding a tracing library to your application.
    What metrics are included in Serverless Workload Monitoring?
    Each active application instance includes an allotment of 20 ingested custom metrics and 20 indexed custom metrics under application monitoring. The APM add-on offering provides 30GB of Ingested Spans and Indexed Spans allotment to 195k. See APM common questions for additional retention periods.
    Can I control how many requests are traced?
    Yes, you can control the percentage of App Service requests that generate APM data by configuring your tracing settings.
    Why are Azure Functions listed in multiple categories (App Services, Functions, and Container Apps)?

    Azure Functions can run on different platforms depending on how they’re deployed, including App Service Plans, Consumption Plans, Premium Plans, or inside Azure Container Apps. Datadog automatically detects the hosting platform and meters usage accordingly:

    • Functions on App Service Plans are counted as App Service instances
    • Functions on Consumption or Premium Plans are counted under Azure Functions
    • Functions inside Container Apps are counted as container replicas

    This ensures accurate usage-based billing, no matter where your functions run.

    How do you define an active application instance?
    Active application instances for Azure Container Apps are the number of unique Container App Replicas that were observed in an active state during at least one 5-minute metering interval, averaged across the month.
    Is Tracing included in Container App Monitoring?
    Tracing Azure Container Apps is supported via the add on Serverless Apps APM product. It can be enabled with the Datadog Serverless Agent and adding a tracing library to your application.
    What metrics are included in Serverless Application Monitoring?

The APM add-on offering provides 30GB of Ingested Spans and Indexed Spans allotment to 195k. See APM common questions for additional retention periods.

    • Functions on App Service Plans are counted as App Service instances
    • Functions on Consumption or Premium Plans are counted under Azure Functions
    • Functions inside Container Apps are counted as container replicas

    This ensures accurate usage-based billing, no matter where your functions run.

    How do you define an active application instance?
    Active instances for Azure Functions are measured based on the number of unique active Container App Replicas that are monitored within each 5-minute period. To calculate the monthly average, we take the average number over all 5-minute periods in the month.
    Is Tracing included in Azure Functions Monitoring?

    What metrics are included in Serverless Application Monitoring?
    Each active application instance includes an allotment of 20 ingested custom metrics and 20 indexed custom metrics under application monitoring. The APM add-on offering provides 30GB of Ingested Spans and Indexed Spans allotment to 195k. See APM common questions for additional retention periods.
    Can I control how many requests are traced?
    Yes, you can control the percentage of Function requests that generate APM data by configuring your tracing settings.
    Why are Azure Functions listed in multiple categories (App Services, Functions, and Container Apps)?

    Azure Functions can run on different platforms depending on how they’re deployed, including App Service Plans, Consumption Plans, Premium Plans, or inside Azure Container Apps. Datadog automatically detects the hosting platform and meters usage accordingly:

    • Functions on App Service Plans are counted as App Service instances
    • Functions on Consumption or Premium Plans are counted under Azure Functions
    • Functions inside Container Apps are counted as container replicas

    This ensures accurate usage-based billing, no matter where your functions run.

    How do you define an active application instance?
    Active instances for Google Cloud Run are the number of unique active application containers that were observed in an active state during at least one 5-minute metering interval, averaged across the month.
    Which Cloud Run workloads are supported and included in the pricing plan?
    Cloud Run services, Cloud Run Functions (Gen 2), and Cloud Run Functions (Gen 1) are included in the pricing plan for both Serverless Application Monitoring and Serverless Application APM. The same pricing applies for all workloads.

The APM add-on offering provides 30GB of Ingested Spans and Indexed Spans allotment to 195k. See APM common questions for additional retention periods.
    Can I control how many requests are traced?
    Yes, you can control the percentage of Cloud Run requests that generate APM data by configuring your tracing settings.
    How do you define an active application instance?
    Active instances for GKE Autopilot are the number of unique active pods during at least one 5-minute metering interval, averaged across the month. Note: If you are using the Datadog Agent to instrument GKE Autopilot, and are using Agent 7.65.0+ and version 3.113.0+ of the Helm chart, ensure the datadog.kubelet.useApiServer property is enabled.
    Are OTel instrumented GKE Autopilot workloads billable?
    For OTel instrumented GKE Autopilot workloads, only Serverless Apps APM is billable. Infra OTel for Serverless will be billable on a future date.
    Is Tracing Included In GKE Autopilot monitoring?

    Common Questions

    What is Datadog Agent Observability and how does it work?
    Datadog Agent Observability helps engineering teams evaluate, improve, and trace AI agents across development and production in one platform. It connects offline experimentation — datasets, experiments, evaluators, and human review — with production observability, including end-to-end agent tracing, quality monitoring, security scanning, and full-stack correlation with backend services and real user sessions.
    What is an LLM span, and how is it different from other spans?
    An LLM span is a single call to an LLM provider such as OpenAI or Anthropic. One agent workflow can generate multiple LLM spans — for example, a retrieval step, a reasoning call, and a tool-use call are each tracked as separate LLM spans within the same trace. Datadog bills only on LLM spans, not on tool spans, retrieval spans, or other workflow spans surrounding the model call. This means you pay for the actual AI work, not every step the agent takes to orchestrate it.
    How does pricing work, and can I retain additional LLM spans?

    The Free tier includes up to 40K LLM spans per month with 15-day retention, unlimited context, and unlimited evaluations — no credit card required. The Pro tier starts at $240 per month on-demand for the first 100K LLM spans, with lower rates at $200 per month month-to-month and $160 per month on an annual commitment.

    For additional LLM spans, we offer the following options:

    1. $3.50 per 10K LLM spans (billed annually)
    2. $4.20 per 10K LLM spans (billed month-to-month)
    3. $5 per 10K LLM spans (billed on-demand)

    Every tier includes the full agent engineering platform from day one, including tracing, evaluations, playground, datasets, experiments, annotations, dashboards, and CLI and MCP access. Extended data retention is available. See “How long is data retained and can it be extended?” for details. Multi-year and volume discounts are also available.

    Do I need to purchase other Datadog products to use Agent Observability?
    No. Agent Observability is a standalone product and can be purchased without any other Datadog subscription. That said, teams that also use Datadog for APM, infrastructure monitoring, or Real User Monitoring gain additional value by correlating agent behavior with services, infra signals, and user sessions — all within the same platform and trace ID, without any extra configuration.
    How quickly can I get started?
    Most teams are tracing agent workflows within minutes. You can instrument using the Python or Node.js SDK, the Java tracer, or via the HTTP API for any other environment. If you use orchestration frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, or LiteLLM, or providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Bedrock, the SDK auto-captures traces with no manual instrumentation required. You can also set up using AI-assisted onboarding via Claude Code or Cursor with a single prompt. Read the documentation.
    Which models, frameworks, and languages are supported?
    Agent Observability supports leading model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Vertex AI, and Bedrock. Agent frameworks supported include LangChain, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, LiteLLM, and Strands Agents. Applications can be instrumented in Python, Node.js, or Java, and teams can bring any custom environment in via OpenTelemetry or the HTTP API.
    Is Sensitive Data Scanner (SDS) included in Agent Observability?
    Yes. Sensitive Data Scanner is built into Agent Observability at no additional cost. For every 10K LLM spans, you receive an allotment of 1 GB of SDS processing. Agent Observability automatically scans, identifies, and redacts sensitive information — including personal data, financial records, and health information — from your LLM application inputs and outputs, helping prevent data leakage before it reaches users.
    How does the Experiments feature work, and is it available to all customers?
    Experiments are included in Agent Observability. You can build versioned datasets from real production traces, run experiments to compare prompts, models, tools, or agent logic side by side, and track results in the Datadog UI or via the SDK. Online evaluations run automatically in production to catch regressions as they happen. Offline, you run structured experiments against curated datasets before deploying. Together they give you confidence that your application performs reliably across both real-world and controlled conditions.
    How long is data retained and can it be extended?

    Trace data is retained for 15 days by default, and trace metrics are retained for 15 months. Experiment results are retained for 15 days by default (3 months with an annual or month-to-month commitment), and datasets are versioned and stored for 3 years so you can always rerun experiments against the same baseline.

    For extended retention, we offer the following retention add-ons:

    • 30-day retention at $6.50 per 10K LLM spans per month (30-day trace retention, 6-month experiment retention)
    • 60-day retention at $8 per 10K LLM spans per month (60-day trace retention, 9-month experiment retention)
    • 90-day retention at $9 per 10K LLM spans per month (90-day trace retention, 12-month experiment retention)
    How is Datadog different from other solutions?
    Datadog connects development and production in one workflow, so teams can experiment with real production data, validate changes before rollout, and trace issues across the full application stack without switching tools. Agent Observability also unifies AI agent behavior with backend services, infrastructure, and real user sessions in the same platform SRE and DevOps teams already use to reduce context switching and speeding root cause analysis.

    Common Questions

    RUM Session Replay RUM Managed Archive Export Pipelines RUM Profiling
    How is a session defined?
    A session is a user journey on your web or mobile application. A session usually includes multiple page views with their associated telemetry.
    When does a session expire?
    A session expires after 15 minutes of inactivity, and its duration is limited to 4 hours. After 4 hours, a new session is automatically created.
    Do I need to purchase both RUM Measure and RUM Investigate SKUs?

    Yes—RUM Measure and RUM Investigate are designed to work together to give you full visibility and cost control.

    • RUM Measure captures all sessions and powers 30+ out-of-the-box performance metrics for your web and mobile apps.

    • RUM Investigate lets you retain only the sessions that matter most—like those with errors, crashes, or high-value actions—based on configurable filters. Retained sessions are stored for 30 days for deep troubleshooting.

    You can also add Session Replay to any retained session for a visual playback of the user experience. Replay sessions are billed separately at $2.50 per 1,000 sessions.

    How long are sessions and metrics retained for?
    The retention policy for RUM sessions and session replays is 30 days. Out-of-the-box metrics are generated on 100% of sessions (RUM Measure SKU) and are retained for 15 months.
    Are the out-of-the-box metrics charged as custom metrics?
    No – Datadog will compute out-of-the-box metrics on the sessions that you send to RUM with the RUM Measure SKU at no additional cost. If you wish to generate your own custom metrics, these will be computed on 100% of your traffic, retained for 15 months, and charged as additional metrics (learn more).
    What mobile platforms and frameworks are supported?

    Datadog RUM supports the following platforms and frameworks:

    • Browser: Vanilla JS, React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, Nuxt, Shopify, and Salesforce
    • Android: Java and Kotlin
    • Apple: Swift and Objective-C
    • Cross-platform frameworks: React Native, Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform, .NET MAUI, and Unity
    • Desktop and connected devices: Electron, Roku, and C++
    Can I view logs from my browser or mobile app in RUM?
    Yes, these logs are automatically tied to the corresponding RUM session, making it easy to monitor when they happen during the user journey.
    How can I begin setting up for RUM?
    Setup steps can be found in our docs: Browser, Session Replay, Mobile.
    How does Session Replay work?
    Session Replay works differently for web and mobile applications. For web ones running on desktop browsers or mobile browsers, it captures changes in the web page code, called DOM and DOM-mutations, to recreate a user’s experience in real-time in the browser. For mobile ones, it flattens the view tree and transforms it into style-rich wireframes, to recompose the UI and end-user’s experience at the right view port.
    How is RUM Managed Archive billed?
    Storage is billed under RUM Managed Archive, per 1,000 stored sessions, at a rate that depends on your chosen storage period — 1, 3, or 6 months. Recovering a session is billed separately, priced at 10x your contracted RUM Investigate rate.
    How long is archived data retained?
    You can choose a storage period of 1, 3, or 6 months, configurable per application. Once you recover a session, it’s available in the RUM Explorer for 30 days.
    Can I search archived sessions from within Datadog?
    Yes. Archived sessions are searchable in a dedicated Managed Archive UI, separate from the RUM Explorer, using attributes like session ID, application ID, account ID, timestamp, user ID, country, service, and version. Search is also possible via API and MCP.
    Do archived sessions count toward my retention filters?
    No, RUM Managed Archive works independently of your retention filters. For a 1-month archive, only sessions not retained by your filters are stored, and once retained sessions are past the standard 30-day retention period, they’re dropped. For a 3- or 6-month archive, every session is stored, but if a session is also retained, its 30-day retention counts as part of that storage period, not on top of it.
    Do I need to be a RUM customer to use RUM Managed Archive?
    Yes. RUM Managed Archive is an add-on to RUM Measure, as part of RUM without Limits.
    How are Export Pipelines billed?
    Export Pipelines is billed at $0.10 per 1,000 sessions, billed annually, as an add-on to RUM Measure.
    Which destinations are supported?
    You can export data to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage.
    Can I filter which sessions get exported?
    You can choose which type of data to export — all RUM event types, or just sessions, views, and actions.
    What format is exported data delivered in?
    Exported data is delivered in either Parquet, which is best suited for loading directly into a warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks, or JSON, which is best suited for custom processing pipelines.
    Do I need to be a RUM customer to use Export Pipelines?
    Yes. Export Pipelines is an add-on to RUM Measure, as part of RUM without Limits.
    How is RUM Profiling billed?
    RUM Profiling is billed at $3 per 1,000 ingested sessions, billed annually. It uses the same session definition as RUM, so there’s no separate unit to track.
    What counts as a billable profiling session?
    A profiling session maps one-to-one to a RUM ingested session. If profiling was active for any part of an ingested session, it counts as one billable profiling session, regardless of duration. Sessions where profiling is enabled but no data is collected are not billed.
    Do I need a RUM plan to use RUM Profiling?
    Yes. RUM Profiling is an add-on to RUM Measure, as part of RUM without Limits.
    Can I profile only some of my sessions?
    Yes. You set a profiling sample rate per application, so you can start small and expand over time. On recent SDK versions, this client-side sample rate can be updated from Datadog Remote Config, in real time, without code changes.
    What platforms are supported?
    RUM Profiling supports profiling for browser, iOS, and Android applications. Use profiling data to identify performance bottlenecks, optimize slow code paths, and improve rendering performance at both the system and code level.
